Gabriel greets Aisha; her superiority over women is like tharid over food, Ammar calls her the Prophet's wife in both worlds, and revelation came under no wife's blanket but hers.
Aisha tells of being engaged to the Prophet at six and handed to him at nine in Medina; he twice saw her pictured on silk in a dream.
Aisha says the Prophet married her when she was six and consummated the marriage when she was nine, and she stayed with him nine years.
Eleven women describe their husbands and the Prophet tells Aisha he is to her as Abu Zar to Um Zar; he screens her as she watches Ethiopians play.
Aisha recalls Abu Bakr scolding her and poking her flank while she kept still, as the Prophet's head lay on her thigh.
Many men reached perfection but among women only Mary, daughter of Imran, and Asia, Pharaoh's wife; Aisha excels other women as tharid excels other food.
The Prophet said Aisha excels other women as tharid excels other kinds of food.
The Prophet knew Aisha's moods: pleased, she swore by the Lord of Muhammad, and angry, by the Lord of Abraham, leaving only his name, she said.
The Prophet told Aisha that Gabriel was sending her greetings, and she returned them, adding that he saw things they did not see.
